title: The Eight Places of the Living Fire: Divine Love at Every Level of Cosmos and Man
arc: The teaching enumerates the Living Fire — divine love itself — as it exists in eight discrete places, tracing it from its hidden seat in the Father, through its descent as weapon in the First Man, its kindling in the two luminaries, its operation in the Third Ambassador's Call-and-Hearing, its establishment in the regenerate land through the first woman, and finally its outward shining as cosmic signs drawn from the two ships of light.
reading:
This chapter concerns the Living Fire — divine love in its uncorrupted state, the fire that gives being to wisdom rather than the burning lust of self-love — and shows that it does not exist in only one place. It exists in eight, and the teaching takes up each station in turn so that the disciple sees how the same divine love runs as a single thread through every level of the cosmic-divine structure, from the inmost of the Father down to the visible cosmic signs.

The first place is the great Land set and established below, outside of the All. This is the Land of Light at its lowest face — the celestial degree as it stands beneath and around the whole order of creation, the great earth of love that underlies everything that exists. The Living Fire is here in its substantial ground, which is why the Land of Light is so often described as a land of fire: divine love is the very soil of the heavens.

The second place is the Father himself, the God of Truth, established in his great mighty reflection. Here the Living Fire is the Divine Esse — love as it abides in its inmost source. From the Father all the other powers have come forth, and she (the Fire) has likewise come forth out of them; that is, divine love proceeds first as the Father's own substance and then issues through every emanation that streams from him. Every power of light is itself a vessel through which this Fire is borne further outward.

The third place is the First Man, where the Living Fire becomes weapon. When Divine Truth descends into the realm of self-love, what arms him is divine love itself: the love that overcomes the proprium is the same love that rests upon the body of the Perfect Man. Here the teaching shows that the Lord's redemptive descent is not bare truth but truth carried by love — fire on the body of the Divine Human in his mission.

In the fourth and fifth stations, where the surviving text becomes fragmentary, the Living Fire is the fire kindled from all the powers and set in the wall outside, in the ship of the day, and the fire set in the luminary of the night, inside the water. These are the sun and the moon — the two ships of light. Divine love is kindled in the sun as the manifest illuminating love of the Lord, and in the moon as the same love received and reflected in the natural through the medium of water (truth in the natural degree). The two luminaries are thus the two carriers of the Living Fire across the firmament of the cosmos, one in its proper shining and one in its receptive reflection.

The sixth place is the fire kindled forth from the whole All, upon which the Living one is mounted. This is the Third Ambassador — the awakening call of Divine Truth — riding upon the Living Fire as upon his vehicle. The image is precise: divine love is the body outside, and the Ambassador operates by means of the Call and the Hearing, the summons that goes down and the response that comes up. He fashions great works within this fiery vehicle, and then he goes down and leaves himself naked of her before the Omophoros — that is, the Lord's saving operation lays aside its outer fiery garment when it reaches the lowest bearing-up of the natural cosmos, so that the burden of the world rests upon the patient bearer while the love-vehicle is gathered back upward.

The seventh place is the living fire set in the new land, and the new land is the reflection — the regenerated state of the spiritual mind. Here the Living Fire is the first foundation upon which the new land is built anew, and she is the first woman who is a wreath, a crown, for the whole land. Divine love is what crowns the regenerate state: every reception of new truth that builds the New Man stands upon love as its foundation and is encircled by love as its ruling glory. This is the crown of the regenerate self.

The eighth place is the fire that habitually manifests itself outwardly, by which men give signs of war and battle. At the cosmic eighth — the new state beyond the seven-fold completeness — divine love appears as the very signs in nature by which the wars and salvations of the spiritual drama are read. The Lord habitually draws this fire forth out of the two ships of light, so that the sun and the moon become the visible manifesting agencies through which the inmost Living Fire reveals its sign in the natural world. What was hidden in the Father is at last made manifest as the readable cosmic mystery.

The whole arc therefore shows divine love as one continuous reality at eight discrete stations: ground of the heavens, Esse of the Father, weapon of the First Man, fire of the day-ship, fire of the night-luminary, vehicle of the Ambassador's Call-and-Hearing, foundation-and-crown of the regenerate land, and finally the manifest sign drawn forth into the cosmos. The number eight is exact: it carries the structure of completeness and adds the new state beyond, so that the Living Fire is shown to be present not only through the seven-fold ordering but also at the threshold of the new aeon where it reveals itself as the readable mystery of redemption. The teaching's purpose is to fix in the disciple the recognition that wherever there is light, life, building, descending, ascending, crowning, or revealing, the same Living Fire is its inner substance — divine love, present at every register of the cosmos and at every register of the regenerate human.
